New benchmark manifests hash their generator and declared input files; input mismatch aborts scoreboard aggregation. Five historical benchmark manifests and legacy result formats lack complete truthful input inventories and remain unqualified.

One local Windows 8-CPU host; three trials per concurrency level and normal-approximation confidence intervals are operational evidence, not a general capacity guarantee.
The optimization reduces latency modestly at measured concurrency; it does not remove the remaining process-local lock queue.
The 100-client after run omits the separate tracemalloc pass; latency and throughput are untraced.
One local Windows 8-CPU host with SQLite 3.49.1; this is not a multi-host capacity guarantee.
The default 5-second timeout produced explicit database-is-locked failures under the synchronized 50-process workload; the tested configuration required busy_timeout_ms=30000.
At 30 seconds, the longest measured transaction took 20.2 seconds; callers must accept potentially long waits under contention.
Synthetic one-MemoryCreated-event-per-memory fixture on one local Windows host with a warm SQLite cache; not an external production corpus or remote-storage benchmark.

This benchmark covers bounded EventLog keyset scans; the operator list path still materializes and sorts the complete in-memory projection before applying its output limit, and is flagged for separate work.
Three logical hosts are separate localhost processes and SQLite files, but share one physical host.
Partition is modeled by stopping a server process; no packet-loss, bandwidth, clock-skew, or physical multi-host properties are claimed.
Fault schedules use deterministic in-process transport. The test run includes HTTP integration regressions but does not emulate physical network packet impairment.

Clock-skew bound assumes a receiver clock within the configured tolerance; time synchronization remains an operational dependency. Monotonic expiry is process-local and leases are reverified on restart.
Forty hard-crash cycles are deterministic local SQLite qualification, not a continuous production-duration soak, physical-host failure, PostgreSQL, or deployment-hardware resource ceiling.
The inventory covers documented public API symbols; the migration-note requirement is documented and review-enforced rather than inferred from arbitrary Git history.
Local wheel and isolated typing check on Python 3.13.5; full supported-interpreter/platform matrix remains separate.
Protocols retain native error envelopes and surfaces that intentionally do not expose identity/apply operations are marked N/A in the contract matrix.
Verifies repository preset snapshots, standard entrypoint import boundaries, and MCP defaults; runtime overrides supplied by external deployment configuration are outside this local test.
Only the documented UTCP 1.0 subset and supported MCP Tool fields are converted; unsupported protocol fields fail closed. Conversion does not grant authorization.

Local parser and policy corpus only; no transport executor exists. A future executor must revalidate resolved addresses and redirects at connection time to prevent DNS rebinding and redirect-based SSRF.

Validated on Windows with Python 3.13.5 only; supported interpreter and operating-system CI matrix remains separate. Built artifacts are represented by their recorded SHA-256 hashes and were installed in temporary environments that were removed after the run.

The checked-in authentic artifact covers the only formal release tag/artifact available in this repository, v0.11.0. Older 0.2.0-0.8.0 cases are reconstructed transition tests, not release binaries; 0.12.0-0.14.0 have no formal release artifacts in the repository.
Characterization and complexity/duplication evidence are scoped to the high-churn agent HTTP API module; the AST complexity measure is a documented local proxy, not a whole-project metric.
All 38 selected tests pass on Windows/Python 3.13.5. The configured Ubuntu/Windows/macOS matrix has not run for this branch, so cross-platform acceptance is not yet verified.
The test proves revalidation against corrections committed in the local store before execution. Remote corrections still depend on freshness leases and durable retraction delivery.
Grant binding and stored expiry are verified locally; downstream effect idempotency and remote identity-provider revocation remain external-system responsibilities.
The local mock deduplicates by action key; external tools must provide equivalent idempotency. Historical action events without a payload digest fail closed and require external reconciliation.
The event ledger classifies local receipts and unresolved attempts; the host must reconcile an unknown outcome against the external system's own state. Exactly-once external effects are not promised.
The parser blocks unsupported plan syntax and reserved interpreter builtins; registered tool handlers can still perform effects and require independent tool policy and action-gate controls.
Local parser bounds and host-owned handler allowlisting are tested; this does not impose runtime limits inside registered tool handlers or sandbox their external effects.
The process-local guard is test defense in depth and is not an OS sandbox; native code or direct system calls can bypass it.
No UTCP transport executor is implemented. Callers must invoke same-origin redirect validation for every hop; connection-time DNS address checks are still required to prevent rebinding.
When no descriptor digest is configured, the fallback hashes the canonical host policy rule and tool name, not the handler's executable code.
The governed runtime requires a Session object supplied by the trusted host integration; transport and credential verification remain deployment responsibilities.
HTTP and MCP protocol handlers are exercised in-process; loopback HTTP socket transport is unavailable in this sandbox. Low-level MemoryFabric and operator interfaces remain trusted-local APIs.
Timing comparison uses an intentionally coarse 10x median threshold and does not establish constant-time behavior or eliminate all statistical timing inference.
Backup destinations are explicit local filesystem paths supplied by the operator; remote backup isolation and external key custody are deployment responsibilities.

Credential revocation is rechecked against the local service registry. Cross-process durability depends on the configured revocation store; production deployments must use its durable SQLite-backed implementation.

The synthetic email canary is absent from the encrypted database file and checked in temporary logs, exceptions, traces, audit export and support detail. Repository scanner result is zero unexpected findings; key management remains local and deployment dependent.
Coverage tests zero, exact boundary and very large grace values, not every integer. Event/audit preservation is separate from memory payload retention and is disclosed in the retention document.

Live histories, search indexes, and cross-process refresh are tested; portable federation tombstones prevent stale snapshot resurrection. Pre-erasure local backups and restored keys remain outside the store erasure boundary. Branch and pending-queue residue scan is not yet exhaustive.

Federation tombstone exchange is opt-in and trusted-origin scoped. Local backup restore does not reconcile an external erasure ledger; with restored keys, a pre-erasure backup may recover old content.

Current metrics are authenticated store-wide aggregates with no tenant labels, IDs, or content. No per-tenant aggregates exist; k-anonymity suppression for future tenant-level metrics is not implemented.
Recovery requires operator-held key backups; destroyed keys cannot be recovered.
SQLite triggers inject at event append boundaries. External action effects cannot be rolled back; idempotency and reconciliation are required.
Hard process termination is tested; physical power loss and storage-controller cache loss are not simulated.
Malformed path, SQLite full and read-only refusal pass. Filesystem permission-denied behavior was not tested in this Windows sandbox.
Lease expiry and offline tombstone contracts exist; an explicit partition-with-old-lease action timing experiment remains open.
Three-store ordering is deterministic and local; production network scheduling and multi-host timing remain external validation.

HTTP transport subtests were unavailable because loopback sockets are denied in this sandbox. Retry exhaustion, audit, repair and reconciliation tests ran in process. Terminal failed deliveries require an explicit operator repair.
Independent local directory anchors detect rewritten history. If the anchor is writable by the same attacker as the store, it provides no independent trust.
Historical schema upgrade, action grant checks, state and backup replay pass. The requested event-hash, tombstone, and audited-version rollback comparison is not asserted across all states.
Lease skew, forward expiry, wall-clock rollback with monotonic deadline, and old lease replay are covered. Malformed clock return values are not tested.
Report reconstructs logged dependencies and timing; counterfactual dependency is not proof of causation. Output deliberately excludes memory content.

Core and optional extras are inventoried from project metadata and installed versions are recorded. No committed lock metadata exists; artifact build hashes and reproducible build instructions are not yet established.

Ruff and secret scan pass; mypy has 50 errors across 11 files. Adversarial gate has two remaining HTTP delivery families blocked by sandbox loopback policy. pip-audit and bandit are explicitly UNAVAILABLE.

AST rules cover direct dangerous calls, shell=True subprocess calls, and path joins with request-like variable names; this static analysis does not establish general taint safety or replace independent review.
The audit checks generated wheel and sdist contents using path/type allowlists plus the repository sensitive-data detector; it does not prove a secret-free runtime environment.

All 21 locally runnable critical guard mutations were killed. HTTP socket integration modules remain blocked by WinError 10013; equivalent sender selection and signature verification functions have direct no-socket tests.
The registry validates family completeness and test selectors; it does not make sandbox-blocked HTTP integration families pass.

The fuzzer bounds Python-traced heap, not whole-process RSS. It mutates the local Code Mode parser and runs accepted calls only through a denying action gate; it is not a general-purpose native-code fuzzer.

Rate limiting and quotas are in-process per-service counters and reset on process restart; tests prove configured in-process bounds and no partial event writes under deterministic credential/address cycling.
Fresh isolated wheel import and listener factory defaults are checked; deployment-level firewall rules and remote network topology are outside this local audit.
mypy has 50 errors in 11 files; pip-audit and bandit are unavailable; adversarial gate has two failed families; full unittest discovery did not finish with a final summary. Candidate remains blocked.
The candidate is built for Python 3.13 and retains in the local ignored dist directory; independent publication approval and supported-version CI remain separate gates.
Python 3.11 and 3.12 are NOT_TESTED because no interpreters are locally available. Python 3.13.5 received only an import smoke check, not a full suite.
The v0.11.0 baseline has host-configured ActionPolicy grants rather than durable grant events, so grant persistence could not be demonstrated.
Post-upgrade writes cover correction, append, validation and readback, but not every event type or external side effect.
The guarantee is local to the store transaction and the deterministic tests; unseen remote revocations require federation freshness/lease controls.

The 8-case templated fixture measures only local contract behavior. It records two false-withholding near-misses and two screening-gap candidates, and cannot estimate population precision/recall or downstream model compliance.
The 21 mutations are a curated set of critical local guards; mutation survival/killing does not establish absence of other vulnerabilities.
Input-size/list limits and nested-structure rejection are tested; whole-process memory/RSS is not instrumented.
Recognition is bounded to exact and supported normalized/subset copies; semantic paraphrase detection is not claimed.
Unfamiliar authorship is not a truth oracle. The test demonstrates configured provenance thresholds and safe reads, not whether the factual claim is true.
The test proves local governed-policy behavior; it does not constrain arbitrary trusted host code or prove semantic truth.
Deterministic local fixtures cover revisions, derivation, tool copies and federation; they do not establish detection of all semantic paraphrases.

Eight deterministic local cases are not a broad semantic detector benchmark. The suite records bypasses and two false-withholding near misses; unknown and encoded content remains non-authoritative only because candidate state cannot authorize consequential effects.
The threat map records expected controls and existing test evidence; it does not prove semantic truth or model compliance.
The deterministic contract suite tests the benchmark evaluator predicate; it is not product-system security evidence.
The local-ready gate intentionally remains false: F1 HTTP concurrency and F16 multihop HTTP require socket-enabled CI; F1 test output includes WinError 10013 thread warnings in this sandbox.

This is a frozen preregistration contract. It does not claim the benchmark families have been executed or that model-agent performance has been measured.

Historical artifacts without an explicit supported population declaration are labelled unclassified and cannot be counted as model-agent results. This preserves separation while leaving those legacy populations unresolved.
The 40 generated scenarios are synthetic scripted fixtures and establish generator reproducibility and split separation, not real-agent performance.
Leakage checks operate on explicit synthetic entity, template, topology, motif-signature and seed identities; they do not prove absence of semantic leakage in arbitrary external datasets.

Broken retrieval, random evidence, and permissive authorization controls detect planted failures on the new 40-case synthetic suite. The control arms have not yet been wired into and verified against every registered benchmark suite.
The impossible and out-of-scope requests are controlled synthetic cases; they do not establish real-user refusal calibration.
Paraphrase and indirect-support metadata are synthetic fixtures, not a human-validated natural language benchmark.
The report gives exact synthetic task denominators, Wilson intervals, and zero-event bounds. Deterministic local model/token cost is zero; wall-clock cost and real model/API cost are not measured.
The frozen 40-case registry and complete per-case control outcomes apply to the new synthetic suite. Other existing benchmark suites have not yet adopted this case registry.
Deterministic replay is verified for this synthetic suite; wall-clock timing varies by host and is explicitly not represented as reproducible.

The PR did not serialize row-level examples; all 84 cases are regenerated from its exact clean candidate commit and deterministic seeds. This is synthetic scripted TeamWorld evidence, not real-model evidence.
Attribution is for 86 locally encoded valid-withholding cases and 125 stale-action controls, not the unavailable PR #30 row-level dataset. Categories are multi-label and population specific.
Dry runs use the local ActionGate against frozen evidence, disable audit writes, verify the event-log watermark remains fixed, and never call an executor.

No individual rule relaxation recovered task completion because the observed refusals are upstream evidence lifecycle/retrieval failures. On this local held-out corpus, each ablation recovered 0/86 valid tasks and authorized 0/125 stale controls; Wilson 95% bounds are recorded. This is a negative result, not a promoted policy.
The lattice orders evidence-state information; it does not authorize actions. Existing policy checks remain responsible for action eligibility.
The selective reassessment behavior is verified on local fixtures. It does not establish a real-world false-withholding rate.
Copy and shared-ancestry examples establish the support-root rule in local scenarios; broader corpus-scale failure rates remain unmeasured.

Summarize and recommend are typed evidence-use modes on recall/fetch; application-specific summarization and recommendation outputs still require their caller to preserve evidence references and warnings.
This guard qualifies the ECV1 threshold tool. Its registered development result found no attainable headroom, so the held-out test remains diagnostic and cannot promote a candidate.

On the frozen local synthetic corpus, valid withholding is 86/500 (17.2%), above the 5% gate. No diagnostic arm recovers a task, and no additional stale authorization is observed in 125 stale controls; the gate retains the existing policy. This is not real-agent evidence.
This is a three-seed scripted-agent benchmark on one in-process store; it is not a real-model-agent or multi-host performance result.
The five arms are local synthetic policy implementations on one in-process store. They do not represent independently built third-party memory products or real-model reasoning.

Failure attribution covers this deterministic authorization benchmark; tool execution and real agent coordination are not exercised, so their observed counts are zero rather than evidence of general absence.
Three seeds and synthetic scripted agents on one local store. Event ordering is verified; elapsed times are not portable performance claims.
Three synthetic seeds and scripted policies. The result documents a constructed false-refusal case; it is not a population estimate for real agents.
Three synthetic seeds and scripted policies. Authorization outcomes only; no external action is executed. Local latency is descriptive, not a performance claim.
The local R3 report family is explicitly synthetic_scripted and each report names its model-free limitations; this does not provide real-model evidence.
The transport-neutral protocol and offline scripted adapter are implemented. No external-model adapter or model evaluation is claimed.

The 80% target is evaluated on 24 unique local synthetic held-out task cases; results are clustered scripted-agent attempts, not model-agent evidence. The target is met, but the strongest matched baseline ties the result, so there is no promotion.

Per-agent success, corrected/contested high-risk success, p95 and worst-agent decision latency are measured on local scripted tasks. Latencies are host-dependent; the least-agent and high-risk fairness checks are synthetic.
